title: The tick comes before the name on every row that has one
goal: On an effect row the tick sits to the right of the name, so you read Blur and then find the switch somewhere after it. The switch is what the row is for, so it belongs first, on the left, with the name beside it. Every row in the panel that has a tick should read that way, in both lists, so the whole panel has one shape.
notes: Reported by the user on 2026-09-07 with a screenshot, saying they asked for this before. An earlier screenshot the same day did show the tick first, so this reversed during that day's work; the row was touched by four commits between noon and half past four, so find which and say so rather than assuming. Today EffectsListInspector.swift line 89 lays the row out as the title at ColorPartLayout.labelWidth then the switch at switchWidth, so the name comes first. The widths live in ColorStylePanel.swift lines 221 and 225 and are shared with the Appearance list, so put the ORDER there too rather than swapping two views and leaving the next list to guess. Note this interacts with an-effect-s-tick-sits-over-the-rule-that-marks-i, which lines the settings rule up under the tick: once the tick is the left column that alignment becomes simple, so whichever lands second should check the other still holds.
acceptance: On an effect row the tick is the leftmost thing, with the name to its right
The same holds for every row in Appearance that has a tick, so the two lists read alike
Rows without a tick keep their names starting on the same line as the names of rows that have one, so nothing looks ragged
The vertical rule marking a row's settings still sits under its tick, which is now the left column
The colours, the controls at the end of the row and everything else keep their columns
The order comes from one shared layout rather than each list arranging its own, so a list added later cannot come out the other way round
Audit written under queue/audits/ with both lists, and rows with and without a tick, anything rough filed as a follow-up

Adversarial review before building: the ask is right and the shortest version is one shared row head, not two swapped HStacks. Cut nothing else. Checked the risk a first-time user would hit: with the tick at the left edge, a row with no tick would start its name a column further left than its neighbours, so tickless rows have to hold the column open or the list goes ragged.

Checked the notes' claim that the order reversed during 2026-09-07. It did not. queue/audits/2026-09-07-appearance-list-two-effects.png, from the 08:46 commit b90ea5c7, already shows the tick AFTER the name, and `git show c72ed55b:Sources/Photonz/PartsInspector.swift` (2026-09-06 12:40, the commit that gave the row its columns) lays out Text then switch. So none of the four afternoon commits did this; the name has led since the row existed.

Built: one PanelRowHead in ColorStylePanel.swift is now the only thing that orders a tick against a name, and both EffectsListInspector and PartsInspector ask it for a head instead of arranging two views. Tickless rows pass EmptyView and keep the column. Opacity and Corner Radius, which are a label over a track rather than a tick and a name, step in by ColorPartLayout.nameLeading.

Adversarial review of the built thing, on a real capture: two things were out of column. The settings under a row sat 9 points LEFT of the names above them, a child less indented than its parent; and a row's reach note started under the tick rather than under the name it explains. Fixed both by deriving OwnedSettings.settingsGap from nameLeading, so the panel now has exactly two left edges. Dropped a readoutLeading constant that nothing used.

Verified on the real app, not by reading: Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/tick-leads-walk.json, status ok, Screen Recording granted so the shots are the real window. Measured the captures pixel by pixel. Ticks at 0, the settings rule at 6 (centred on the 14 wide tick), and every name in both lists at 24.5 to 26 (the spread is glyph bearing). Appearance and Effects agree, and the arrow, whose rows have no tick at all, still starts its names at 24 with its swatch in the same column as a rectangle's. Scripts/test.sh green, 4700 tests.

Acceptance item 4 is met, which also answers the blocked sibling an-effect-s-tick-sits-over-the-rule-that-marks-i: its decision card offered 'the tick leads the row' as option a, and the user filing this task chose that in effect. The rule now hangs under the tick. Not touching that task's status from here.

The tick leads every row in both panel lists, ordered by one shared PanelRowHead so a later list cannot come out reversed. Tickless rows hold the column open, and the settings rule now hangs centred under the tick.
